content.text: The excerpts compare British and American railroad safety, emphasizing British collisions versus American derailments and bridge failures, then discuss architecture, ornament, art, religion, and representations of water. They also recount Elsie Inglis’s Scottish Women’s Hospitals: founded in Edinburgh, operating in France, Belgium, Serbia, Russia, and Romania, including Royaumont, Kragujevatz, Mladenovatz, Krushieevatz, Reni, Odessa, Galatz, and Braila. Inglis died after returning to Newcastle and was buried in Edinburgh. A final historical section describes Dellon’s imprisonment in Goa’s Inquisition, his transfer through Bacaim to Goa, confinement in cells, appearance at an auto-da-fé, and Buchanan’s later visit to the same Inquisition.
